items.scene: A space probe sent images of a rocky object orbiting the Sun. The first images showed no tail. A student called it a comet because it was in space. Her partner asked for evidence of ice or a tail before accepting that label. They agreed to collect more observations.
items.prompt: Which statement is an observation rather than a guess?
options: Every space object is a comet.
The object must be made of ice.
items.why: A lack of a visible tail is recorded in the images. The other statements add information not observed.
items.hint: Separate what the text says from what you can only guess.

items.title: Unit 1 · Vocabulary, Grammar & Reading
items.scene: A space probe sent images of a rocky object orbiting the Sun. The first images showed no tail. A student called it a comet because it was in space. Her partner asked for evidence of ice or a tail before accepting that label. They agreed to collect more observations.
items.prompt: What does the partner’s response show?
items.answer: A scientific label should be supported by evidence.
options: A scientific label should be supported by evidence.
A first guess is always correct.
No-tail images prove that comets never have tails.
items.why: The partner asks for observations that distinguish the label, rather than accepting a label just because the object is in space.
items.hint: Separate what the text says from what you can only guess.
